To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep abstaining classifiers are a novel type of neural network with a novel loss that allows the network to learn to abstain on examples that are difficult for the network to classify.
we introduce the deep abstained classifier -- a deep network trained with a loss function that allows it to abstain on difficult or noisy examples.

we propose a deep abstaining classifier that can be used for robust learning in the presences of label noise, and that we provide theoretical analysis of the loss function and automatic tuning of accuracy/coverage trade-off for the deep abstaining classifiers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning from noisy labels, and we propose a novel loss function to address this problem.
learning in the presence  of label noise.
developing deep neural network models that can learn when they don’t know.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deep abstaining classifiers are an important and useful addition to the deep learning toolbox.
the deep abstaining classifiers have the ability to identify and ignore confusing examples, and thus learn more robust models.
the deep abstaining classifiers are a promising approach for learning in the presence  of structured or unstructured label noise, and also for learning an out-of-category detector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deep abstaining classifiers provide a novel and effective approach to learn in the presence of noisy labels or out-of-category samples.
we propose a new learning algorithm for deep neural networks that can learn in the presence of noise and learn to abstain on difficult examples.
the DNN can be trained to identify the examples that it does not know, and abstain on them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a well designed loss function for deep neural networks enables learning to abstain, and that this abstention can lead to improved performance on the non- abstained samples.
abstaining classifiers can be trained with deep neural networks and that they can be used to identify and learn from structured noise, as well as identify out of category examples.
a deep neural network can be made to learn to abstain on difficult-to-learn samples, thereby improving performance on the remaining samples.
